ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the detector on the hot air balloon indicates that the angle of depression from the bottom of the hot air balloon at point $A$ to the top of a building is $30^\circ$, and the angle of depression to the bottom of the building is $60^\circ$. The distance from point $A$ on the hot air balloon to the ground is $150m$. What is the height of the building in meters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw $AH\perp BC$, extending through point $CB$ to $H$,\\
In right $\triangle ACD$,\\
$\because \angle CAD=30^\circ$, $AD=150m$\\
$\therefore CD=AD\cdot \tan 30^\circ=150\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=50\sqrt{3}(m)$,\\
$\therefore AH=CD=50\sqrt{3}m$\\
In right $\triangle ABH$,\\
$\because \angle BAH=30^\circ$, $AE=50\sqrt{3}m$\\
$\therefore BH=AH\cdot \tan 30^\circ=50\sqrt{3}\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=50(m)$,\\
$\therefore BC=AD−BH=150−50=\boxed{100}(m)$

The distance from point $A$ on the hot air balloon to the ground is $150\text{ m}$. What is the height of the building in meters?
raw_record.answer: Solution: As shown in the diagram, draw $AH\perp BC$, extending through point $CB$ to $H$. In right $\triangle ACD$, $\because \angle CAD=30^\circ$, $AD=150\text{ m}$, $\therefore CD=AD\cdot \tan 30^\circ=150\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=50\sqrt{3}(\text{m})$, $\therefore AH=CD=50\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$. In right $\triangle ABH$, $\because \angle BAH=30^\circ$, $AE=50\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$, $\therefore BH=AH\cdot \tan 30^\circ=50\sqrt{3}\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=50(\text{m})$, $\therefore BC=AD-BH=150-50=\boxed{100}(\text{m})$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point A on the left is located below the hot-air balloon, and from A to ground point D is a vertical line segment; on the right is a building, with the bottom as C and the top as B, and BC represents the building height. At A there is a horizontal dashed line as a reference line for the angle of depression, line of sight AB points to the top of the building, and line of sight AC points to the bottom of the building. The figure marks the angle of depression from the horizontal line to AB as 30°, to AC as 60°, and the vertical distance AD from A to the ground as 150 m. Reasoning: Let the horizontal distance from the building to A's vertical projection point D be DC = x. Because the angle of depression of AC is 60°, in right triangle ADC, tan 60° = AD / DC = 150 / x, so x = 150 / tan 60° = 150 / √3 = 50√3. The building top B and bottom C are on the same vertical line, so the horizontal distance from A to B is also 50√3. Because the angle of depression of AB is 30°, the vertical drop from A to B is x tan 30° = 50√3 × √3/3 = 50 m. Therefore the building height BC = the total height from A to the ground AD − the drop from A to B = 150 − 50 = 100 m.
